Dr Christine Hodges
2 Hill Forest Road
Newtown

11 February 2019

Dear Dr Hodges

Re: Mr John Aloisius
DOB: 04/09/1985

Thank you for seeing Mr Aloisius, who has recently been diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis. He is now ready for discharge and follow-up at your clinic.

Mr Aloisius was admitted to the ED on 01/02/2019 with a recent history of productive cough with hemoptysis. Additionally, he had fever and night sweating. His oxygen saturation was 92%. Examination revealed cachexia and scattered rales were auscultated. The diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis was confirmed after observing apical lung infiltrates on an X-ray, and detecting a positive culture for mycobactrium TB. 

During hospitalisation, Mr Aloisius was placed on respiratory isolation room and TB medications were subsequently commenced along with vitamin B-6. The nursing team ensured adequate diet and use of medications. 

Today, Mr Aloisius’s condition has significantly improved, with a negative myocobactrium culture. 

Please note, Mr Aloisius will be discharged on the following medications; pyrazinamide, ethambutol, isoniazide and rifampin for two months. After that, he should continue isoniazide and rifampin for additional four months.He should also continue taking vitamin B-6.

Kindly montior Mr Aloisius for medication compliance, check his serum creatinine and liver enzymes for drug toxcitiy and assess his visual acuity and red-green color perception with an Ishihara test.

Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely

Doctor.
